habitat: Primary lowland rainforests; hill dipterocarp forests; swamp forests; and mountain forests
story: The Rhinoceros Hornbill (Buceros rhinoceros) is an extraordinary bird that belongs to the Bucerotidae family. It is most commonly observed in Primary lowland rainforests; hill dipterocarp forests; swamp forests; and mountain forests, where its behaviors contribute to the ecological dynamics of the area. Listed as Vulnerable (VU) by the IUCN, this species' future depends on continued conservation action. The story of the Rhinoceros Hornbill is one of adaptation and resilience, offering valuable lessons for conservationists. This poster aims to bring the Rhinoceros Hornbill into focus, highlighting its beauty and the importance of its habitat.
